Theopompus: Ancient Greek Historian and Rhetorician


Theopompus (unknown–314 BCE) was a renowned ancient Greek historian, rhetorician, and student of Isocrates. As a prominent figure in the Hellenistic era, his works significantly contributed to the development of historiography and rhetoric.


A prolific writer, Theopompus authored numerous historical accounts, including ' Philippica', which chronicled the reign of Philip II of Macedon and its impact on Greek politics. His writings not only provided insight into the complexities of ancient Greek society but also showcased his mastery of rhetorical skills.


Theopompus' legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing later historians like Plutarch and shaping the narrative of the Hellenistic period. His emphasis on empirical research and attention to detail set a new standard for historical writing.


As a testament to his enduring impact, Theopompus remains an essential figure in the annals of ancient Greek history, offering valuable perspectives on the intricacies of power, politics, and culture in the ancient world.
